blocks.text: Lots and land in Big Bend

items.t: The defining fact: land in Big Bend is in the provincial Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), administered by the Agricultural Land Commission, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan supports protecting and expanding agriculture in Big Bend. The City runs a Burnaby Farm Tour Map for the Big Bend farming district, promoting farm-gate and nursery sales, and states Big Bend has a culturally diverse farming heritage, with historic Chinese Canadian small-scale farms that still exist today.
Farm stock character: working farms and nurseries in the A1 agricultural district, including the historic Chinese Canadian small-scale farms the City documents.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the research documents Big Bend's farmland as ALR land and the district as the City's main agricultural area; it does not publish a parcel-count or hectare split between ALR farm ground, industrial ground and the Riverside residential pocket, so no ALR percentage split is stated. ALR status and permitted farm / non-farm uses for a specific property are checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder before any value is priced in.
Servicing position for farm ground: Do not assume urban servicing standards reach a foreshore parcel; confirm with the City and the ALC for the parcel.

River employment lands: the wider Big Bend / south Burnaby river lands also carry industrial use — industrial space accounts for nearly half of Burnaby's employment space city-wide in the City's employment lands work, with the Big Bend sub-area accounting for much of it on the City's assessment geography; that assessment figure is a City-study geography, not the MLS® sub-area boundary.
Commercial/industrial land tax treatment: Not confirmed: — the research is silent on a commercial/industrial land tax position for Big Bend parcels, and none is filled in here.

No bare-land strata plan in Big Bend was verified: Stated for the record: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure (Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply to the lot) — no plan of that form is documented for this district, whose farm and rural-residential stock is freehold in character.

No named bare-land development, subdivision offering, assembly or rezoning proposal in Big Bend was verified: Burnaby Fraser Foreshore Park is the district's named public landmark — City park and dyke land, not development inventory.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Big Bend

items.t: Big Bend is in the City of Burnaby, BC — the City's main agricultural area in south Burnaby, on the Fraser River foreshore flats below the city's steep south slope. "Big Bend" is the GVR board sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report under community "Burnaby", and it matches the name the City of Burnaby itself uses for its south Burnaby agricultural area. (SnapStats, September 2026)

Nearby areas: South Slope and Garden Village above the bluff to the north, Edmonds to the north-east, the Glenlyon / Byrne Creek industrial lands within the wider south Burnaby employment area, and Richmond across the North Arm of the Fraser River to the south.

Roads and transit: Marine Way / Marine Drive runs along the top of the foreshore flats and Byrne Road and Sussex Avenue descend to the river lands; Highway 1 and the Edmonds / Metrotown town centres are north up the slope. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

The nearest library branch is the Tommy Douglas Branch, 7311 Kingsway, up the slope in Edmonds (Burnaby Public Library has four branches, one in each quadrant). The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health), in central Burnaby. Farm-gate and nursery sales in the Big Bend farming district are promoted on the City's Burnaby Farm Tour Map; a main shopping centre in the area is not confirmed on an official source: Not verified — everyday shopping is up the slope in Edmonds and South Slope.

Schools: public schools are run by School District 41 (Burnaby), which operates 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide; SD41 has no middle-school tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12). No completed locator run is documented for this ground. School names are Ministry-listed names, spelled exactly.

Market context, labelled correctly: Burnaby IS a SnapStats-covered community, and SnapStats has NO land category — the figures here are labelled community/sub-area context only, never land figures. Burnaby community detached median $1,825,000 and condos & townhomes median $686,000. Sub-area medians are not verified (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Big Bend

items.t: Zoning — Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815 (in effect July 1, 2026): the new Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, and the City is updating zoning regulations for agricultural districts through that rewrite. A1 is the City's agricultural zoning district in Big Bend (chickens may be kept in the A1 district under Zoning Bylaw rules). Parcel-level minimum lot sizes and the current district for a specific Big Bend farm parcel: Not verified — an A1 assumption from the old bylaw is not enough for a farm purchase; verify the current zoning district in writing with the City and the ALC.

Subdivision + servicing — process documented, base number HELD not confirmed: subdivision of a Big Bend parcel runs through the City's subdivision process under its subdivision servicing bylaw framework, with servicing standards confirmed with the City for the specific parcel and, for ALR parcels, ALC approval engaged first (below).

ALR block — the governing rules for Big Bend farm ground: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. ALR status and permitted farm / non-farm uses for a specific property are checked in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder, and ALR land is governed by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission Act framework — run the ALR check first on any farm parcel, before pricing development or non-farm value into it.

Floodplain diligence — the second defining fact: the City states Burnaby's southern boundary borders nearly 7 km of the North Arm of the Fraser River and the nearly 800 hectares of low-lying area between the steep south slope and the Fraser River is a floodplain; the Fraser River poses a substantial flood hazard from snowmelt in late spring and early summer and from combined heavy rain and winter storm surge events. The City protects the lowland areas with river and shoreline dykes, pump stations and flood boxes, maintains a Flood Response Plan, and receives regular updates from the BC River Forecast Centre during flooding events and freshet. Confirm the parcel's flood construction requirements, dyke position and insurance before subjects come off, not after.

Burnaby property taxes and farm class: City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date. Farm-class assessment and tax treatment for a specific Big Bend parcel is a BC Assessment / tax-notice check per property: Not verified here — confirm farm-class status and what transfers with the sale, because the tax treatment drives the carrying cost. Burnaby's published 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, sewer use and garbage fees for residential properties; farm and industrial utility charges for a specific Big Bend property: Not verified.

blocks.text: Good to know about Big Bend

items.t: The district's farmland has a named heritage, not just a reserve boundary: the City states Big Bend has a culturally diverse farming heritage, with historic Chinese Canadian small-scale farms that still exist today — a working-farm landscape the Burnaby 2050 OCP supports protecting and expanding, promoted to buyers at the farm gate through the City's Burnaby Farm Tour Map.

"Nearly half the city's employment space" is a study geography, not this sub-area's boundary: the City's employment lands work puts industrial space at nearly half of Burnaby's employment space city-wide, with the Big Bend sub-area accounting for much of it on the City's assessment geography — a figure a seller may quote as if it measured the MLS® sub-area; it does not, and the research flags the distinction itself.

Rural-residential lots (Riverside): A fee-simple Riverside lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Servicing position for farm and industrial ground: the district is dyke-protected lowland with pumped drainage as part of the City's flood-protection system; parcel-level water, sewer and utility servicing for a specific Big Bend farm or industrial property: Not verified — farm and industrial utility charges for a specific property are likewise not verified. faq.q: Is Big Bend a residential neighbourhood where I can buy a building lot?
faq.a: No — on the City's own sources it is primarily an industrial and agricultural district: ALR farmland, river industrial lands, a foreshore park and a small rural-residential pocket (Riverside). There is no subdivision housing market and no verified lot offering; residential buying here means an existing Riverside home on its lot.

faq.q: Is the floodplain a real cost, or a formality?
faq.a: Real. The district is a roughly 800-hectare Fraser River floodplain protected by dykes, pump stations and flood boxes, with flood hazard from late-spring/early-summer snowmelt and from combined heavy rain and winter storm surge. Confirm flood construction requirements, dyke position and insurance before subjects come off.

faq.q: What actually trades here as land?
faq.a: Farm parcels on ALR land (the core of the district), industrial parcels and buildings on the river employment lands (worked in process terms only), and rural-residential homes in the Riverside pocket.

faq.q: Can I subdivide or build a second home on a Big Bend farm?
faq.a: Start with the ALR, not the city: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, ALR residences cannot be stratified, and residence caps apply (principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² on parcels 40 ha or less / 186 m² over 40 ha). Then verify the parcel's current district under Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, in effect July 1, 2026) in writing — agricultural-district rules were being updated through the rewrite.

faq.q: How do I check what a farm parcel is allowed to do?
faq.a: In the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder — confirm ALR status, permitted farm uses and any non-farm-use restrictions before pricing development or non-farm value into the property. The same check runs first on any industrial parcel with an ALR edge.

Yes — land in Big Bend is in the Agricultural Land Reserve administered by the Agricultural Land Commission, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan supports protecting and expanding agriculture there.

faq.q: Is Big Bend in a floodplain?
faq.a: Yes — the City states the nearly 800 hectares of low-lying land between Burnaby's south slope and the Fraser River is a floodplain, protected by river and shoreline dykes, pump stations and flood boxes, along nearly 7 km of the North Arm of the Fraser River.

faq.q: What kinds of properties are in Big Bend?
faq.a: Working farms and nurseries on ALR land, industrial properties on the river employment lands, and rural-residential homes in the Riverside pocket — plus Burnaby Fraser Foreshore Park on the river.
